description:
Make a materialized callable value carry exactly one coherent publication contract, and let the now-impossible multi-surface ambiguity become unrepresentable rather than silently arbitrated.

Reframed by the f98.6 finding: this is the natural consequence of fixing the f98.6 root, not a separate arbitration to build. Once one published transport boundary resolves to one native callable boundary BY CONSTRUCTION (f98.6: collapse the reducer's over-specialized `[]`/`any` resolutions to the boundary's joined surface), the multi-surface / multi-boundary condition these fallbacks exist to paper over can no longer occur. So the work is deletion, made safe by the upstream invariant.

Findings that stand:
- deterministic_callable_boundary_fallback (native.rs, first_class_publication_boundary's Err arm) is DEAD across the corpus + lib + adversarial stressors: select_inhabited_callable_boundary is only ever called with a single candidate; a panic mutation in the Err(()) arm leaves the matrix green.
- Polymorphic indirect closures already dispatch correctly through the heap closure's stored code pointer (opaque_fn_value_join passes interp/run/build), so no first-class dispatch boundary needs building.
- The genuine multi-surface condition is reachable only at the sibling settled_callable_boundary consumer, and it is driven by the f98 root -- it disappears once f98.6 lands.

Required work (do AFTER f98.6 establishes one-resolution-per-boundary):
- Delete deterministic_callable_boundary_fallback and its comment; collapse the now-unreachable Err(()) arm of first_class_publication_boundary into a loud incomplete_native_program error matching settled_callable_boundary.
- native_codegen/driver.rs build_codegen_callable_boundaries (debug_assert_eq! at ~922) and build_codegen_closure_targets (~940, ~971): with one boundary per id and one coherent surface per target, these become real one-per-key invariants -- make them fail loud (release-safe), not debug_assert_eq! that the first of two diverging surfaces silently wins in release.
- Regression: the same returned/captured closure invoked indirectly at more than one callable surface; existing direct-target coverage stays green.

Checks: cargo test --lib; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; full fixture matrix green.
title: Delete dead callable-boundary fallback; fail-loud on multi-surface surface divergence
